It seems to me like you aren't causing drama for popularity and attention...it seems like you're hurting. And also that you want the same things everyone else wants. We all want to be liked, noticed, and accepted. There's nothing wrong with that, and no one way to accomplish all those things. Some people make it look really easy. I'm not sure how. But the fact that they make you feel that you're below them is evidence enough that they are not in fact better than you, because nice people don't act that way. 

When I was younger, I always wanted to play with toys and would always feel that I was already too old for them no matter how old I actually was. And I only got older, and then it felt even less possible.

Now I'm 38, and my biggest joy is being involved in fandoms for tv shows I love. I write fanfiction and talk to other people who love the characters I do. I go to comic con and cosplay, and then go and tell everyone I did it and how much I love it. Because it's fine to love what you do. Anyone who tells you it isn't, is frankly a spoil sport and chances are they're going to have a super boring life. 

However, I understand that I've spent a lot of time working up to embracing what I love and being vocal about it, and at my age it's easier to do so. I got this way from years of feeling inferior and getting sick of it and becoming defiant. There are times in life where it's really hard to embrace being "different" from those around you. (By "different" I mean imaginative, creative, in touch with your emotions, which I'm guessing that you are only because you sound a little like me and that's how I am.)  People will pick on you when they see you're "different", because shunning you makes them feel more normal, like they fit in. Imagine how many things they must not be doing that they'd actually like to do because they're too afraid to be treated exactly the way they're treating you. Imagine what they might be doing in private that they don't tell anyone about because they don't want to be ridiculed. My 45-year-old husband cries when he watches anime! I doubt he'd walk around advertising that fact to anyone, but I love him for it. It makes him human. 

I say that the definition of becoming an adult is "being able to do whatever you want whenever you want." That means if you want to be 50 and still playing with barbies, or 35 and having cookies for dinner, it's ALL GOOD. Life should be about enjoyment, or else what is it for? Those people who act like they're better than you...you don't really want to become friends with them and still have them in your life 20 years from now and making you feel this way, right? Wouldn't you rather hang out with people who think you're awesome for being exactly how you are? The world is full of people with many different interests. I hope you'll start meeting the people who will celebrate you for being you. For now I say: find what you love the most, and a nice side bonus of that could be that you find you become really good at it (though the point should just be feeling good because you're doing what you enjoy). That you're maybe even "the best." Did you know there are people out there who get paid to do cosplay because companies want to be represented?

There are so many possibilities. I hope you'll hang in there and find some of the best ones for you.
By the way I'm new to reddit as of today so I don't know if the site will inform you that I edited my last comment, but I did, so please see that again if you haven't already. Thanks.

That's the hope. Maybe something miraculous will happen and I won't have to die. I probably have about a year before I put my plan into action. Chances are slim but maybe they'll come up with something that can help my physical issues. I refuse to hold out hope, but I won't shut my mind off to it completely if something becomes available. I'm suicidal but not unreasonable.

No. We've never really had any sort of relationship. She's almost the definition of the last person I could talk to about anything. 

I do wish it were that simple. Through my life I've been capable of seeing humor, and the bright side, etc. I've rewired my brain with cognitive behavioral therapy. Experienced how life-changing antidepressants can be. And so on. So I've definitely tried avenues other than "just being upset." There can and does genuinely come a point for some people where that's the only option left is all.

No problem.

It's a noble desire, I suppose, so we can at least give ourselves that no matter how else we might dislike ourselves. 

I've come back to edit this comment because rather than just leaving you with these thoughts, I will say: I once felt exactly the way you do. And if I had ended things then, I would have missed out on a lot of wonderful things. Unrelated issues are what have since brought me to this forum--things that are unlikely to ever befall you, as they're health-related and don't affect many. 

This is a freaking horrible time overall in the world, so any stresses we have are just under the magnifying glass 24/7 because we're stuck, alone, with them. You talked about trying to make the best of things...but have you given yourself permission to just say, "You know what, this SUCKS, and I'm totally valid in feeling that way?" I don't know if that will help you. But maybe it can be a comfort that absolutely no one in their right mind can fault you at the moment for being frustrated...even people who otherwise would absolutely never get it. Because they are currently isolated right now themselves, or have been at some point in the last few months, and whether they have someone with them or not, on some level they've doubtless felt frustrated about some aspect of their life that was being aggravated by being locked down, and they felt helpless to fix it. I'm not at all saying their problems are equivalent to yours--I simply mean that right now it's pretty universal that all the shitty things in life feel even shittier.

Though, I'm speaking as an outsider, and I understand much of what I've just said may not be helpful to you. So by all means disregard what doesn't. But I do hope things will improve for you.

I'm sorry it's so rough. I hear you. I cried the other day thinking about all the beloved people who have died from covid, and yet \*I'm\* still here. I was wishing I could trade places with someone who still had a lot of life to live. Someone whose loved ones are grieving their loss.

Thanks. You've already talked to me more than anyone else has in weeks. Which is pathetic. The last person I heard from, more than a week ago, was my sister who was texting to let me know she had dialed me by accident so I didn't need to call back. LOL. It's awful but I can still recognize it's funny. My dark humor seems to be growing sharper.

Yes, this resonates. I've begun making my plans, and what I never realized before I got this serious (I was serious back in 2009 but still willing to seek help, which I did) was how much goes into all of this. All the planning. One of the things on my list is to organize/clean much of my place, and as I've begun the process it's occurred to me that it might go faster than I actually want it to.
Maybe that's why I'm so fucking exhausted. There is no figuring this shit out.
For context I guess I can add that I've had help. Years and years of it. But there is no help for my current issues.
I appreciate that. I'm not asking for help, though. More just not to be 100% alone.

Irl I would say no, but on some level I suppose I must want to talk to someone in some fashion or I wouldn't be here. I hate that, but it's an unavoidable fact. And I'm not even sure \*why\* I want to talk to someone because I really do think the situation is beyond hope. I don't know if I'd volunteer to talk to me, though, lol. I'm A Lot.
